name: MOCAK
funding: Municipal museum of the City of Kraków, with a car-dealer partnership.
records_note: Partner logos are undated and the Museum Council is named, but no reports are posted; the city bulletin with accounts timed out.

name: Modern Art Museum of Fort Worth
funding: 2025-26 grants include Sid W. Richardson Foundation, Ben E. Keith Foundation, Bank of America Charitable Foundation, City of Fort Worth and Texas Commission on the Arts. Corporate: Frost, Headington Companies.
watch: Sid W. Richardson's oil fortune funds its foundation, which gave in 2025-26. Fort Worth police seized Sally Mann photographs in January 2025; no charges followed.
records_note: Names funders under a 2025-2026 grants heading but posts no annual report, accounts or board; Form 990 filings for 2001 to 2025 sit on ProPublica.

name: Modern Art Museum of Yerevan
funding: Small museum founded in 1972 with the city's backing and listed among Yerevan municipality's museums; its current funder roster is not published.
watch: First Soviet museum devoted to modern art; director Nune Avetisyan.
records_note: No annual reports, accounts, funder list or board found on the museum site; the team page lists the director and staff only.

name: Moderna Galerija (MG+MSUM)
funding: National museum funded by the Slovenian Ministry of Culture.
records_note: Its public-information page posts annual reports 2020 to 2024 in the AJPES finance format and names the council, but lists no sponsors.

name: Moderna Museet
funding: SEK 271M income (2025), state 70%. Sponsors: Bank of America, Bloomberg, PwC, Jung, Patriksson and an unnamed wine and spirits supplier; partners Hotel Skeppsholmen and Panasonic Connect.
watch: Sponsor Bloomberg: more than 260 UK artists asked five London theatres to drop Bloomberg Philanthropies in May 2026. Moderna Museet was not named.
records_note: It posts annual reports 2015 to 2025 with accounts, names sponsors and partners on its support page, and lists its Board of Trustees.

name: MoMA PS1
funding: $18M annual operating budget. Subsidiary of The Museum of Modern Art; supported by NYC Department of Cultural Affairs, MoMA Board, and foundation grants.
watch: Leon Black still a trustee after Epstein payments; Fink, Crown and Dubin named in Strike MoMA and the 2024 sit-in.

name: MOMus
funding: State museum group under the Greek Ministry of Culture.
records_note: No annual report, accounts or sponsor list found; the about page names the management board chair, vice chair, seven members and the general director.

name: Monash University Museum of Art
funding: University-funded; Besen family built the 2010 Caulfield premises; Ian Potter Sculpture Court commissions; media partner Schwartz Media; MUMA Contemporaries from $1,000.
watch: Censorship row: on 25 Mar 2025 Monash indefinitely postponed Stolon Press: Flat earth (Khaled Sabsabi) under pressure; it reopened 29 May 2025.
records_note: MUMA posts no reports of its own; parent Monash University publishes an annual report with accounts, and MUMA names donors on its support pages.

name: Montresso Art Foundation (Jardin Rouge)
watch: Residency on a 10-hectare olive grove 20 km outside Marrakech, hosting about 40 artists a year; visits by appointment.
records_note: The foundation's site posts no reports, accounts, funder list or board; it names only collaborating institutions and its Amis de Jardin Rouge association.

name: Morgan Library & Museum
funding: $31.4M expenses (2023); J.P. Morgan endowment, JPMorgan Chase (top corporate donor), Morgan Stanley, AIG, law firms, NYC and NYS funds.
watch: Banking founding fortune. Bloomberg Philanthropies is a Leader-level corporate supporter (list current as of 28 Jul 2025).
records_note: Annual Reports to Donors run 2004 to 2024, a dated corporate supporter roster is public, trustees are listed, and 990s are on ProPublica.

name: Mori Art Museum
funding: Corporate endowment from Mori Building Co., Shiseido, corporate sponsors.
watch: Cultural initiative of a real-estate developer, with a corporate circle of luxury and financial firms.

name: Mosaic Rooms
funding: Fully funded by the A.M. Qattan Foundation to date. Al-Qattan Charitable Trust paid for the 2026 refit and is the family foundation's largest donor. Independent charity since February 2026.
watch: Qattan wealth comes from Kuwaiti construction. Director Pip Day's 2024 dismissal from a Concordia gallery concerned a film screening, not funding.
records_note: No annual reports found; accounts are on the Charity Commission register, the footer names Al-Qattan Charitable Trust undated, and eight trustees are listed.
